full_judgment:
6. Learned Senior Assistant Judge, Rangpur awarded decree of permanent injunction in favour of plaintiffs and restrained defendants from entering into schedule Kha property i.e. the suit property forcibly or from dispossessing plaintiffs thereon. The Judgment and Decree is dated 28-5-1991. In awarding decree learned Senior Assistant Judges as trial Judge considered evidences of the parties, both oral and documentary. Learned trial Judge found that defendants or their predecessors got no connection with the property recorded in Cadestral Survey and State Acquisition Khatians. Learned Trial Judge held that plaintiffs produced series of Rent Receipts manifesting payment of rent with respect to suit property and plaintiffs could prove possession over suit property through testimonies of witnesses. Learned trial Judge found that cause of action for laying the suit had been proved. Learned trial Judge found that in a suit of this nature there was no need of discussion of title over suit property and thus did not feel necessity of considering arguments put forward from side of defendants. Learned trial Judge ultimately found that plaintiffs got exclusive possession and prima facie title over the suit property. 

 7. Defendant Nos. 1 to 3 felt aggrieved of the above adjudication and sought setting aside same through a medium of appeal being Other Appeal No. 83 of 1991 in the Court of District Judge Rangpur, Learned Sub-Judge and Artha Rin Adalat No. 1 Rangpur heard the appeal and by Judgment and decree dated 29-11-1992 allowed it, set aside Judgment and decree recorded in Other Suit No. 104 of 1990 and dismissed the suit. In recording dismissal, learned appellate Judge being the last and final Judge of fact considered evidences both oral and documentary and other materials on record. Learned appellate Judge taking into account Exhibit-Kha and Kha-1, Cadestral Survey Khatian Ras. 69 and 94 found that property of those two Cadastral Survey Khatians stood recorded in the names of Sreeman, son of Ram Singh, Rajani, son of Lili, in four annas equ-al share. Learned appellate Judge taking into consideration of Exhibit- Kha and Kha(1) also found that name of the father of Sreeman Barman was Ram Singh. Learned appellate Judge on consideration of testimonies of DWs 3, 5 and 6 and also testimony of PW 2 found that all of them substantially supported the case of defendants that Sreeman, LiIi, Dip and Rai Chand were full brothers and son of Ram Singh. Learned Appellate Judge found that PW 1 himself admitted that entry in Cadestral Survey Khatian Nos. 69 and 94, Exhibit-Kha and Kha(l) were true entries. Learned Appellate Judge also found that there was no explanation from the plaintiff side as to why the land of Cadestral Survey Khatian Nos. 69 and 94 had been recorded in four ann as equal share in the name of Sreeman and successor of Lili, Rai Chand and Dip Chand. Learned Appellate Judge on assessment on the testimony of PW 2 and DWs3 and 6 positively found that at the time of alleged pattan in 1346 BS Plaintiff Kailash was a mere infant of 8/9 years of age. Learned appellate Judge also on a careful scrutiny of Rent Receipts Exhibits- 3 to 3(Ga) found that Rent Receipts had not been written and signed by Kailash Chandra who was a boy of 8/9 years of age and a student of class-IV Learned appellate Judge also noted that hand writing and signature appeared to be of the product of matured hand. Learned appellate Judge also found that Rent Receipts had been purposely created subsequently collecting those. Learned appellate Judge discarded the claim of plaintiffs that Kailash granted settlement of his share of lot Nos. 1,2 and 3. Learned appellate Judge also found that Revisional Settlement Record of Right published in the name of plaintiff No.1 in sixteen annas share was wrong and without foundation. Learned appellate Judge on assessment of the testimonies of witnesses of both the parties found that testimonies of defendant's witnesses were more reliable and trustworthy than the testimonies of the witnesses for the plaintiffs. Learned appellate Judge, thereafter, found that exclusive possession of plaintiffs over the suit property had not been proved. Learned appellate Judge recorded positive decision that defendant had been able to establish their co-sharership in the suit jotes and the claim of plaintiffs exclusive possession over the suit property did not arise. Further positive decision rendered by learned Judge is that defendants got joint possession over suit property. 

 11. This Court in the exercise of Civil Revisional Jurisdiction under section 115 of the Code can interfere with the decision of an appellate Judge only when it is shown that decision is based on gross misreading of evidence or non-consideration of the material evidence of decision had been founded on misconception and misapplication of law or misinterpretation of any material document or otherwise it is perverse being contrary to evidence and materials on records and also law. Learned Subordinate Judge and Artha Rin Adalat No. 1 as the appellate Judge and also the final judge of fact appears to have considered pleadings and evidences adduced from both the sides and materials brought on record. Learned appellate Judge on consideration of legal evidences both oral and documentary found that Dip Chand Rai Chand, Sreeman and Lili, the heirs and successive heirs of Ram Singh alias Jogot Chandra Barman used to reside on the suit property and their successors were residing thereon. Further decision rendered was that the land of cadastral survey Khatian Nos. 69 and 94, Exhibit-Kha and Kha-1 stood recorded in four annas equal share in the names of Sreeman, LiIi, Rai and Dip Chand Barman and defendants could establish their co-sharership in the suit jote they got joint possession over suit property. This decision has been founded on legal evidences and materials brought on record and this decision does not appear to have been based on misreading or non-consideration of the evidences nor mis-interpretation of any material document and the same appears to have been rested on proper reading and consideration of the evidences and true interpretation of the material documents produced from both sides. In cannot be also suggested that those decisions reached by learned appellate Judge suffers from manifest perversity.
